Nix 2.35.2 evaluated the pinned flake and built the x86_64-linux package with the normal optimized release profile, doCheck=1, one Cargo job, one Nix job/core. Release compilation completed in 23m50s; buildPhase was 24m17s and checkPhase was 37m56s. Exact final command (also in active-runner.sh and verified against the live process):

```
nix --extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes' build path:/source --no-link --keep-failed --max-jobs 1 --cores 1 --option sandbox false -L
```

Preflight command was `nix --extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes' flake check path:/source --no-build --option sandbox false`. The preflight evaluates x86_64-linux; it explicitly reports that aarch64-linux and aarch64-darwin were omitted as incompatible systems. Their separate native Rust/package receipts are not inferred from this Nix run. Nix's own sandbox was disabled inside the task-owned Docker container; the build used the existing normal locked/offline Cargo hooks. No tests or package checks were disabled.

Exact output from result-path.txt:

```
/nix/store/xxj8dq7ln66sgydnmxgwys6li4lxld7c-zap-faster-0.30.0
```

Final derivation: `/nix/store/pvfn50a8km4xr4vj9sy0waja0i5zh6qg-zap-faster-0.30.0.drv`. Generated derivation data is preserved in derivation.json.

The installed executable reports `zap-faster 0.30.0`. Actual output checks verified executable permissions, the LD_LIBRARY_PATH runtime wrapper, exact desktop Icon=zap-faster and StartupWMClass=zap-faster, a nonempty scalable SVG icon, a nonempty Omarchy theme template and executable Omarchy hook. installPhase and fixupPhase both completed, including RPATH shrinking, script interpreter patching and stripping. The earlier disposable install/wrapper fixture is recorded separately and was not substituted for these actual gates. No GUI or hardware was opened, and this proves the package output rather than attended NixOS desktop, camera/audio or linked-account runtime.

## Corrections and preservation

The initial actual build failed because v4l2-sys-mit could not find linux/videodev2.h. Adding the official rustPlatform.bindgenHook to the flake's development shell and package native inputs resolved the missing header. Its complete failed proof is retained at H:/Scratch/Codex/zap-nix-final-before-bindgen-fix.

The next actual build passed all normal tests but failed installPhase because the copied Windows CRLF flake embedded carriage returns in shell hooks. The flake and its scoped Git attribute were normalized to LF. Both generated shell hooks passed bash -n and contained zero CR; shipped desktop, template and executable Omarchy hook also contained zero CR. That full failed receipt is retained at H:/Scratch/Codex/zap-nix-final-bindgen-crlf-failure. Final corrected build repeated the normal build and tests and completed successfully. No Rust/product source changes were made during these Nix corrections.

# Native ARM64 synthetic startup and memory receipt

Three accepted app runs completed with exit 0 on 2026-10-11. Median elapsed capture-and-exit proxy: **0.73 seconds**. Median application peak RSS: **176.35 MiB** (180,584 KiB). No repository source edits or Cargo compilation were performed.

| Run | App capture-and-exit elapsed | Peak RSS, KiB | Peak RSS, MiB | PNG | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0.79 s | 180,584 | 176.35 | 1280x800 | 0 |
| 2 | 0.73 s | 181,132 | 176.89 | 1280x800 | 0 |
| 3 | 0.71 s | 180,404 | 176.18 | 1280x800 | 0 |

## Method and scope

The immutable final native Linux ARM64 executable was run in a disposable Ubuntu 22.04 task helper on the MacBook's Docker VM, bounded to one CPU, 1 GiB memory and zero swap. Networking was disconnected before the accepted runs. Each run received new HOME, XDG config/data/cache/runtime and TMP directories. Xvfb provided an isolated 1600x1200 display; Mesa software rendering was selected. GNU time -v wrapped only the application, excluding Xvfb startup:

```
/usr/bin/time -v -o run-N/time.txt /input/zap-faster --demo --demo-shot run-N/startup.png --demo-size 1280x800 --demo-shot-delay 0
```

The dataset is the built-in offline Messages demo in src/demo.rs, default dark theme, selected Ada Lovelace synthetic conversation. This is not the separate 100-chat/10,000-message archive profiling dataset. All three PNG signatures and dimensions were verified on Windows, and all three images were visually inspected: chat list, message bubbles, document/voice/link cards and composer are present. The synthetic image thumbnail is still blurred in this first requested frame. The image is not blank, and this receipt does not claim fully settled asynchronous media.

All three PNG SHA256 values are c0dcb0da00b3dfca92b5d496f5cc869c34331f98d2294ba10c13ad9c81a2c30d. The executable SHA256 before and after is unchanged: 298414d65f8a22c49b5cc89da7fd46043d3c3c8f4c833aaa7d4dc885027fed41.

Elapsed time measures process start through the first requested PNG capture and process exit. It does not separately timestamp first window presentation. It does not measure real-account archive startup, initial phone sync, network recovery, old Intel hardware or Windows performance. App directories are cold; the operating-system file cache was warm and was not cleared. Binary hash verification and an earlier preflight warmed that cache. The binary retains its normal debug build profile. These conditions prevent a cold-boot or release-build performance claim.

Raw GNU time reports, app logs, exit receipts, PNGs, binary hashes and resource bounds are beside this report; results.json and validated-pngs.json contain machine-readable results. A preliminary app run succeeded, but its subsequent validator failed because python3 was absent; that attempt is retained under python-validation-attempt-run-1 and is excluded from the three accepted samples. PNG validation was moved to the Windows host. App logs have ordinary Xvfb XSETTINGS/physical-size warnings, with no panic or ERROR-level failure. Cgroup memory peak was 1,073,741,824 bytes including cache/provisioning/hash work; memory.events max was already 9,466 and remained unchanged across the three accepted samples. OOM and OOM-kill counters remained zero. Application RSS is the GNU time measurement above, not the cgroup cache peak.

## Quantitative recovery fairness evidence

Existing fixture backend::worker::background_history::tests::full_mode_rotates_beyond_ten_chats_and_preserves_daily_budget (src/backend/worker/background_history.rs:284) asserts exact round-robin ordering for 60 successful requests across 12 synthetic chats. Each receives exactly 60 / 12 = **5 requests**; maximum/minimum service ratio is **1.0**. Restoring the checkpoint also preserves the exhausted 60-request daily budget. The fixture passed in H:/Scratch/Codex/test-default-call-final.log:550. No compilation or fixture rerun was needed for this reconciliation. This quantifies scheduler fairness under a virtual clock, not phone/network latency or recovery throughput.

Together with the earlier Windows synthetic archive ingestion/reopen/peak-working-set receipts and passing persistence/backoff fixtures, this fills the locally runnable native-client startup/RSS and numeric scheduler-fairness evidence. Attended real-account sync and actual-device runtime remain separate verification boundaries.

Cleanup: after evidence was copied and inspected, the verified idle task-owned helper codex-zap-arm64-startup-20261011 and its disposable committed image codex-zap-arm64-startup-20261011:1 were removed successfully. The original stopped ARM build container, its caches, and all host proof files were preserved.

limitations: Local receipts reused for matching inputs; no attended phone/device proof, publication or installed-client replacement.
